answer: Divergent-History Challenge. Each identity publishes a short random zephyr seed with every action; the protocol anchors its acceptance on a chained history hash that must differ across identities. Clones forced to replay an identical history produce matching hashes and are rejected at validation. Honest agents keep unique seeds as an ivory marker of provenance. An attacker must run each clone through an independent interaction history, paying full compute and latency per identity rather than copying one.
